relations.note: Etzel hosts, patronizes, and campaigns alongside Dietrich.
Dietrich resides at Etzel’s court as an exiled military leader.
Atli lures Gunnar and Högni to his court with deceitful promises.
Gunnar resists Atli's demand for the treasure and fights his forces.
Atli has Gunnar cast among serpents after he refuses to reveal the treasure.
Atli discovers Gunnar's affair with Oddrún and destroys Gunnar and Högni.

relations.myth: Feast and catastrophe at Etzel's court
relations.note: Etzel hosts the fatal feast but does not order Gunther's death.
Modern scholars sometimes equate them or reconstruct them as cognate champions.
Bödvar defends Hrólfr and dies fighting beside his king.
relations.source: Gesta Danorum II and Hrólfs saga

relations.note: Bödvar enters Hrólfr’s service and becomes his paramount champion.
Dietrich opposes Kriemhild’s faction and delivers his captives alive to her.
Guðrún is falsely accused of sleeping with Þjóðrekr and is vindicated.
Dietrich defeats, binds, and delivers Gunther alive to Kriemhild.
Dietrich defeats, binds, and delivers Hagen alive to Kriemhild.
Gunnar gives his sister Guðrún in marriage to Sigurd.
Kriemhild orders the captive Gunther beheaded during her revenge.

relations.myth: Gunnar's imprisonment after the Niflung battle
relations.note: In the saga's hybrid tradition, Grímhild urges Gunnar's captors to dispose of him.
Guðrún attempts to warn Gunnar of Atli's treacherous invitation.
After Gunnar's death, Guðrún avenges her brothers by destroying Atli.
Guðrún is Gunnar's sister in the Norse tradition.
Hagen counsels Gunnar, rescues him, and joins his final attack on Walter.
Gunnar and Högni induce Gothorm to murder their oath-brother Sigurd.
The brothers resist Atli and conceal the Niflung treasure's location.
Hagen kills Gunther during their struggle over the ring.
Hagen serves Gunther, murders Siegfried with his assent, and guards the hoard.
Högni is Gunnar's brother in the Norse genealogical tradition.
Helgi kills Sigrún’s father during the war against Höðbroddr.
Saxo’s Helgo fathers Roluo Kraki with Urse.
Sigmundr is Helgi’s father in the received Eddic and Völsung genealogy.
Sigmundr names Helgi and grants him estates and a sword.
Helgi is Signý’s nephew through Sigmundr; no direct interaction is recorded.
Starkaðr is listed among the enemy allies mobilized against Helgi.
Signý preserves and assists Sigmundr throughout their long campaign against Siggeirr.
Signý’s honey stratagem enables Sigmundr to kill the she-wolf and escape the stocks.
Signý conceals Sigmundr’s sword in straw, enabling him and Sinfjǫtli to escape burial.

relations.myth: Signý conceives Sinfjǫtli in magical disguise
relations.note: Disguised as another woman, Signý sleeps with her unwitting twin for three nights.
Signý and Sigmundr are Vǫlsungr and Hljóð’s eldest children and twins.

god_relations.note: Beowulf grapples with Grendel unarmed and tears off his arm.
Beowulf mortally wounds Grendel by tearing away his arm and shoulder.
Bödvar fights the supernatural army raised by Skuld against Hrólfr.
Bödvar dies during the night attack organized by Skuld.
The dwarf Alfrikr assists Dietrich against Grim and supplies heroic equipment.
Alfrikr provides equipment associated with Dietrich’s victory and heroic career.
Egil reproaches the sea powers associated with Rán for taking his son.
Alberich fathers Gunther's maternal half-brother Hagen, who manipulates and kills Gunther.
Sigurd swears brotherhood with Gunnar and Högni after joining their household.
Gunnar's household benefits when a potion makes Sigurd forget Brynhild and marry Guðrún.
Shape-changed Sigurd crosses Brynhild's fire in Gunnar's form and wins her.
Unable to break his oath personally, Gunnar plans and authorizes Sigurd's killing.
Gunther promises Kriemhild to Siegfried in exchange for help winning Brunhild.
Invisible Siegfried supplies the strength while Gunther appears to defeat Brunhild.
Gunther assents to Siegfried's murder, joins the false hunt, and conceals responsibility.
Gunther participates after Hagen's potion makes Siegfried forget Brünnhilde and woo her.
Gunther participates in Hagen's plot to murder Siegfried.
Brynhild becomes Gunnar's wife through Sigurd's deceptive surrogate wooing.
Gunnar marries Brynhild after Sigurd crosses the fire disguised as him.
Brynhild pressures Gunnar to arrange Sigurd's death after discovering the marriage fraud.
Brunhild becomes Gunther's wife in the German tradition.
Gunther appears to defeat Brunhild's deadly athletic trials using invisible Siegfried's strength.
Gunther obtains marriage and consummation through Siegfried's concealed assistance and force.
Brunhild overpowers Gunther, binds him, and hangs him from a wall peg.
Gunther seeks Brünnhilde while Siegfried, disguised as Gunther, subdues and abducts her.
Wagner makes Hagen Alberich’s son, unlike every medieval tradition.
Alberich commands Hagen to obtain the Ring for him.
Hagen lunges after the Ring; the Rhinemaidens reclaim it as he dies.
The valkyries accompany Sigrún and protect Helgi’s fleet and army.
In the opera, Hervör kills the invented beloved Vidar.
Skuld is Hrólfr’s half-sister, born to Helgi and an elfin woman.
Skuld attacks Hrólfr with human and supernatural forces, using sorcery to cause his defeat.
Sigmund descends from Odin through Sigi, Rerir, and Völsung.
Odin, disguised as a one-eyed stranger, plants the sword that Sigmund alone draws.
Odin confronts Sigmund with his spear and shatters Sigmund's sword.
An unnamed ferryman, probably Odin, takes Sinfjötli's corpse from Sigmund and vanishes.
Frigg joins Odin in enabling the birth of Sigmund's father Völsung.
Wagner makes Siegmund a direct son of Wotan.

god_relations.myth: Nothung planted in the ash tree
god_relations.note: Wotan plants Nothung for Siegmund to draw from the tree.
Wotan withdraws his protection, shatters Nothung, and enables Siegmund's death.
Fricka condemns Siegmund's incest and compels Wotan to withdraw his protection.
Disguised as Starkad’s foster-father, Odin grants lifetimes, victory, wealth, poetry, weapons and noble esteem.
Starkad dedicates Víkar to Odin by hanging and stabbing him.
A praise-stanza lists Starkad among giants whom Thor struck or overcame.
Thor tears four arms from Saxo’s six-armed Starkad, leaving him human-shaped.
Thor curses Starkad with crimes, wounds, poverty, dissatisfaction, lost poetry, popular hatred and childlessness.

Agnarr.note: Áslaug treats her stepson’s death as requiring vengeance like her own child’s.
Bjarki kills Agnarr after the challenger’s sword breaks.

Alphart.note: Alphart is Dietrich’s young retainer, treacherously killed by Witege and Heime.

Angantýr.note: Starkad kills Angantýr while supporting Helgo against nine brothers.

Angantýr Arngrímsson.note: Hervör I is the posthumously born daughter of Angantýr.
Hervör summons Angantýr from his barrow and compels him to surrender Tyrfingr.

Angantýr Heiðreksson.note: Hervör II is the sister of the Gothic king Angantýr.
Angantýr receives news of Hervör II’s death and laments his sister.

Angantýr Hǫfundarson.note: Hervör I is the mother of Angantýr Hǫfundarson.

Angantýr’s eight brothers.note: Starkad kills Angantýr’s eight brothers while aiding Helgo.

Angantýr’s eleven brothers.note: Hervör summons the dead berserkers and threatens them if Tyrfingr is withheld.

Arngrímr.note: Hervör I is Arngrímr’s granddaughter through Angantýr.

Atli's mother.note: Transformed into a serpent, Atli's mother bites Gunnar through the heart.

Aðils.note: Bjarki joins Hrólfr’s conflict and expedition against the Swedish king.

Beigaðr.note: Beigaðr and Bödvar fight jointly among Hrólfr’s champions.

Bemon.note: Bemon becomes Starkad’s Viking companion after Víkar’s death.

Bera.note: Bera is Bödvar’s mother and directs him toward his inheritance.

Biterolf.note: Biterolf is a heroic associate within Dietrich’s connected tradition.

Bjarmarr.note: Hervör I is Bjarmarr’s maternal granddaughter and grows up at his court.
Bjarmarr fosters Hervör, who later returns to his court after raiding.

Bjǫrn.note: The bear-cursed prince Bjǫrn is Bödvar’s father.

Bjǫrn járnsíða.note: Bjǫrn is named among Áslaug’s sons.
Bjǫrn participates in the revenge campaign initiated by Áslaug.

Blindr inn bǫlvísi.note: Blindr detects Helgi’s unusual strength but accepts Hagall’s misleading explanation.

Borghildr.note: Borghildr is Helgi’s mother in the Eddic and saga genealogy.

Brynhildr Buðladóttir.note: Áslaug identifies Brynhildr as her mother.

Brünhild.note: Brünhild belongs to the heroic complex incorporated into Dietrich’s saga.

Brünnhilde.note: Brünnhilde defies Wotan and tries unsuccessfully to save Siegmund in battle.

Dagr Hǫgnason.note: Helgi spares Dagr and accepts his oath after killing Dagr’s kin.
Dagr breaks his oath and kills Helgi with a spear lent by Óðinn.

Dancrat.note: German tradition makes Dancrat Gunther's father.

Dankwart.note: Dankwart fights under Gunther as a Burgundian companion and relative.

Dietleib.note: Gunther, Gernot, and Hagen attack Dietleib before a later reconciliation.
Gunther's conflict with Dietleib's company ends in reconciliation.

Dietmar.note: Dietmar or Þetmarr is Dietrich’s father in German and Norse traditions.

Dietrich.note: Dietrich defeats and captures Gunther and Hagen after the hall battle.
Gunther joins the Worms champions opposing Dietrich's company.

Ecke.note: Dietrich reluctantly kills the giant Ecke after a brutal prolonged duel.

Eggerich.note: Eggerich is a dwarf associated with Dietrich’s Sigenot adventure.

Eirekr.note: Áslaug treats her stepson’s death as requiring vengeance like her own child’s.

Elg-Fróði.note: Elg-Fróði is Bödvar’s elder, animal-marked brother.
The brothers test their strength before exchanging counsel and a death-token.

Ermanaric.note: Dietrich’s usurping uncle or kinsman dispossesses him and provokes repeated wars.

Eyjólfr.note: Helgi kills Eyjólfr, a son of Hundingr, in battle.

Fasolt.note: Ecke’s brother or companion confronts Dietrich.
Some versions make Fasolt accommodate himself to or join Dietrich.

Frakki.note: The pirate’s departure is contrasted with the continuing companionship of Starkad and Bemon.

Friðþjófr.note: Starkad and Víkar defeat Friðþjófr during their military campaigns.

Fróðmarr.note: Fróðmarr fosters Hervör II in England in the R recension.

Geirþjófr.note: Starkad fights Geirþjófr as an enemy during Víkar’s campaigns.

Gernot.note: Gernot is Gunther's brother and co-king in German tradition.
Gernot fights beside Gunther and dies in the Hunnish catastrophe.

Gibeche.note: Rosengarten A makes Gunther a son of Gibeche.

Gibich.note: Wagner makes Gunther the son of Gibich.

Giselher.note: Giselher fights Dietrich’s retainers and is killed by Wolfhart.
Giselher is Gunther's brother and co-king in German tradition.
Giselher fights beside Gunther and dies in the Hunnish catastrophe.

Gjúki.note: Norse tradition makes Gunnar the son and dynastic heir of Gjúki.

Glaumvör.note: Glaumvör is Gunnar's wife in later Norse versions.
Glaumvör recounts ominous dreams and warns Gunnar against the fatal journey.

Glámr.note: Grettir wrestles the monstrous revenant through the hall and roof.
Grettir decapitates Glámr and burns his corpse.
Glámr curses Grettir with arrested strength, misfortune, outlawry, isolation, and fear of darkness.

God.note: Beowulf credits God with victories and the opportunity to win treasure.

Gothorm.note: Gothorm is Gunnar's younger brother or half-brother in prose systematizations.
Gunnar induces and drugs the non-oath-bound Gothorm to kill Sigurd.

Granmarr.note: Helgi kills Höðbroddr’s father in HH II’s battle summary.

Grendel’s mother.note: Beowulf fights the avenging monster after pursuing her beneath the mere.
Beowulf beheads her with a gigantic sword found in her hall.
The film reinvents her as a seductive shape-shifter who takes Beowulf as lover.
The film creates a sexual relationship absent from the medieval poem.

Grim.note: Dietrich kills the giant Grim with Alfrikr’s assistance.

Gríma.note: Áslaug curses Gríma after years of concealment, degradation, and abuse.

Grímhild.note: Norse prose makes Grímhild Gunnar's mother.

Grímr.note: The later Starkad descends from Grímr, son of Álfhildr and the giant Starkad.

Gullrönd.note: Some Norse prose systematizations include Gullrönd among Gunnar's siblings.

Gullväg.note: Gullväg desires Hervör while believing her masculine identity Hervardur.

Guðmundr Granmarsson.note: Guðmundr belongs to the enemy host and reports Helgi’s invasion.

Guðmundr of Glæsisvellir.note: Guðmundr receives Hervör and arranges or approves her marriage to Hǫfundr.

Hadburg.note: Hagen steals Hadburg’s clothes and forces her to prophesy.
Hadburg falsely predicts success so Hagen will return her garments.

Hadubrand.note: Hadubrand knows Dietrich as the lord for whom his father fled.

Hagall.note: Helgi’s foster-father shelters him and explains away his strength while disguised.

Haki.note: Haki and Bödvar fight jointly among Hrólfr’s champions.

Haklangr.note: Haklangr and Bödvar fight jointly among Hrólfr’s champions.

Halfdan.note: Saxo makes the fused Danish Helgo a son of Halfdan.

Halga.note: Modern scholarship proposes identifying the Beowulf Scylding Halga with Helgi.

Hallmundr.note: The supernatural wilderness being shelters and assists Grettir.

Hama.note: Starkad kills the Saxon champion Hama after a difficult fight.

Hamall.note: Hamall is Helgi’s foster-brother by implication through Hagall’s fosterage.
Helgi uses Hamall’s identity while secretly spying in Hundingr’s hall.

Harðrefill.note: Harðrefill and Bödvar fight jointly among Hrólfr’s champions.

Hatherus.note: Hather avenges his father by decapitating Starkad in exchange for Starkad’s gold.

Heime.note: Heime challenges Dietrich and is defeated before joining him.
Dietrich recruits Heime, who also provides him the horse Falke.
Heime later opposes Dietrich’s party and helps Witege kill Alphart.

Heimir of Hlymdalir.note: Heimir conceals Áslaug in a harp and transports and sustains her.

Heiðrekr.note: Hervör I is the mother of Heiðrekr.
Hervör gives or transmits the inherited sword Tyrfingr to Heiðrekr.
Hervör protects Heiðrekr’s patrimony after he kills his brother.
Hervör II is a daughter of Heiðrekr.

Helche.note: Etzel’s queen protects Dietrich and supplies treasure for his warriors.

Helgi Haddingjaskati.note: HH II declares Helgi Haddingjaskati to be Hundingsbani reborn.

Helgi Hjǫrvarðsson.note: The prose framework implies Hundingsbani is the rebirth of Helgi Hjǫrvarðsson.

Helgo.note: Saxo’s Danish Helgo combines Scylding genealogy with Hunding and Hothbrodd victories.

Herkja.note: Herkja falsely accuses Guðrún of sexual relations with Þjóðrekr.

Herrad.note: Dietrich marries Herrad, who is also associated with his final return.

Hervör II.note: Hervör I is Hervör II’s paternal grandmother.

Herþjófr.note: Starkad and Víkar avenge Haraldr by killing his slayer Herþjófr.

Hild.note: Young Dietrich kills the giantess Hild.

Hildebrand.note: Hildebrand serves as Dietrich’s tutor and weapons-master.
Hildebrand is Dietrich’s chief counselor, retainer, and exile companion.
Hildebrand kills Sigenot and frees the imprisoned Dietrich.
Hildebrand belongs to Dietrich's company opposing Gunther's Worms champions.

Hildegund.note: Gunnar pursues the escaping Hildegund and Walter for their treasure.

Hjalli.note: Gunnar identifies Hjalli's trembling heart and knows it is not Högni's.

Hjalti.note: Bödvar rescues Hǫttr from abusive retainers and protects him at court.
Bödvar gives Hǫttr courage, stages his victory, and makes him Hjalti.
Bödvar and Hjalti fight together and knowingly die beside Hrólfr.

Hjörvarðr.note: Bödvar fights the rebel forces commanded by Hjörvarðr.
Hjörvarðr.source: Gesta Danorum II and Hrólfs saga

Hjǫrvarðr.note: Helgi kills Hundingr’s son, whose name varies between poem and saga.

Hljóð.note: The wish-maiden Hljóð is Sigmund's mother.
Signý is the daughter of Vǫlsungr and Hljóð.

Hlöðr.note: Hervör II and Hlöðr are paternal half-siblings.
Hlöðr’s Hunnish army overwhelms Hervör II’s fortress and kills her.

Hringr.note: Hringr, king of Upplönd, is Bödvar’s paternal grandfather.
Hringr is summoned with his sons among Helgi’s enemies.

Hringr’s sons.note: Hringr’s unnamed sons are summoned among the forces opposing Helgi.

Hrothgar.note: Saxo makes Ro the brother of his fused Danish Helgo.

Hrímnir.note: The giant Hrímnir is Sigmund's maternal grandfather through Hljóð.

Hrómundr.note: Hrómundr and Bödvar fight jointly among Hrólfr’s champions.

Hundingr.note: Helgi kills the enemy king and thereby earns his Hundingsbani epithet.
Helgi orders the dead Hundingr to perform degrading domestic and animal-tending chores.

Hvít.note: Bödvar kills Hvít in vengeance for cursing and destroying his father.

Hvítserkr.note: Hvítserkr is named among Áslaug’s sons.
Hvítserkr joins the revenge expedition initiated by Áslaug.
Hvítserkr and Bödvar fight jointly among Hrólfr’s champions.

Hámundr.note: Hámundr is Helgi’s full brother in the saga’s synthesized genealogy.
Hámundr is Signý’s nephew through Sigmundr; no direct interaction is recorded.

Hávarðr.note: Helgi kills Hundingr’s son; poem and saga preserve different names.

Hímnir.note: The giant Hímnir is Signý’s maternal grandfather through Hljóð.

Höðbroddr Granmarsson.note: Helgi opposes Höðbroddr’s unwanted betrothal to Sigrún.
Helgi kills his rival Höðbroddr during the decisive battle.

Hœmingr.note: Helgi impersonates Hamall, then sends Hœmingr a taunting revelation.

Hǫfundr.note: Hervör I marries Hǫfundr and bears him two sons.
Hervör opposes Hǫfundr’s attempt to dispossess or permanently exile Heiðrekr.

King Isung.note: Dietrich’s heroes compete against King Isung’s champion-band.

Kárr inn gamli.note: Grettir enters Kárr’s mound and wrestles the animated corpse.
Grettir defeats and decapitates the revenant Kárr.
Grettir takes treasure and a sword from Kárr’s mound.

Künhilt.note: Künhilt helps Dietrich and his companions escape Laurin’s captivity.

Landvættir of Norway.note: Egil curses the land-spirits, ordering them to wander until his royal enemies leave Norway.

Laurin.note: Dietrich violates Laurin’s garden, contests its toll, and battles the dwarf king.
Laurin magically overcomes and imprisons Dietrich and his companions.
Reconciliatory versions make the defeated Laurin Dietrich’s subordinate or ally.

Leifr.note: Helgi’s shipmaster Leifr is ordered to count the assembled fleet.

Norna-Gestr.note: Norna-Gestr witnesses and narrates Starkad’s encounter with Sigurðr.

Oddrún.note: Oddrún is Gunnar's clandestine lover because Atli refuses their marriage.
Gunnar summons Oddrún by harp, but she hears remotely and arrives too late.

Odilia.note: Odilia is Þiðrekr’s mother in the saga genealogy.

Odoacer.note: Otacher’s hostility drives Dietrich and Hildebrand eastward into exile.

Orkise.note: Dietrich’s side overcomes the heathen oppressor Orkise.

Ormarr.note: Ormarr serves beside Hervör II at the Gothic frontier fortress.

Ort.note: Etzel entrusts Ort to Dietrich, but Witege kills the young prince.

Osid.note: Gunnar fights Atli's nephew Osid and is captured by him.
Osid captures Gunnar and places him in a fatal tower or snake-tower.

Rutha.note: Biarco marries Rutha, Rolvo’s sister, after Agnerus’s death.

Rüdiger of Bechelaren.note: Rüdiger is Dietrich’s fellow leader at Etzel’s court.
Dietrich laments Rüdiger after the latter is killed.
Rüdiger hosts Gunther and his company and becomes their in-law.
Obliged by Etzel, Rüdiger becomes Gunther's battlefield opponent.

Rǫgnvaldr.note: Rǫgnvaldr is Áslaug’s son in the saga’s five-son genealogy.

Scharpfe.note: Etzel entrusts Scharpfe to Dietrich, but Witege kills the young prince.

Sibich.note: Sibich’s malicious intrigue helps cause Dietrich’s persecution and war.

Siegfried.note: Dietrich’s rage and supernatural heat overcome Siegfried during their duel.
German tradition briefly mentions Gunther and Brunhild's son named Siegfried.

Sigelind.note: Sigelind reveals that all Burgundians except the chaplain will die.

Sigenot.note: The giant Sigenot defeats and imprisons Dietrich.

Siggeirr.note: Signý is unwillingly married to Siggeirr, king of Gautland.

Siggeirr.myth: Signý exchanges appearances with a sorceress
Siggeirr.note: Signý substitutes a disguised sorceress in Siggeirr’s bed without his knowledge.

Siggeirr.myth: Vengeance and the burning of Siggeirr’s hall
Siggeirr.note: Signý engineers the revenge culminating in Siggeirr’s death when his hall is burned.

Sigi.note: Sigi is Signý’s great-grandfather in the Völsung genealogy.

Sigrún Hǫgnadóttir.note: Sigrún is Helgi’s valkyrie lover and wife and bears his unnamed sons.
Helgi defeats Höðbroddr after Sigrún asks him to prevent her unwanted marriage.
Sigrún protects Helgi’s fleet and army as a valkyrie.
The dead Helgi returns for one night and sleeps in Sigrún’s arms.

Sigurd Svein.note: Isung’s champion fights within the tournament cycle opposing Dietrich’s heroes.

Sigurðr Fáfnisbani.note: Áslaug identifies Sigurðr as her father.
Sigurðr is Helgi’s paternal half-brother only through the combined saga genealogy.
Sigurðr is Signý’s nephew through Sigmundr and is born after her death.
Sigurðr strikes the aged Starkad with Gramr and knocks out two teeth.

Sigurðr ormr í auga.note: Áslaug bears Sigurðr, whose serpent-eye validates her claimed ancestry.
Sigurðr first answers Áslaug’s call to avenge his half-brothers.

Sinfjötli.note: Sinfjötli is Helgi’s paternal half-brother in the combined Völsung genealogy.
Sinfjötli campaigns with Helgi and conducts the flyting on his behalf.

Sinfjǫtli.note: Signý bears Sinfjǫtli after conceiving him with her twin brother Sigmundr.
Signý tests Sinfjǫtli, sends him to Sigmundr, and employs him as her avenger.

Sons of Swerting.note: Starkad incites Ingeld to kill Swerting’s sons in vengeance for Frotho.

Starkaðr Áludrengr.note: The later Starkad descends from his eight-armed giant namesake through Grímr and Stórvirkr.

Starólfr.note: Starólfr and Bödvar fight jointly among Hrólfr’s champions.

Stórvirkr.note: Stórvirkr is Starkad’s father in both Icelandic and Saxonian genealogical traditions.

Svipdagr.note: Svipdagr and Bödvar fight jointly among Hrólfr’s champions.

Swerting.note: Starkad pursues vengeance against the family of Swerting, Frotho’s killer.

Sísarr of Kiev.note: Sísarr wounds Starkad in single combat, but Starkad ultimately defeats him.

The Christian God.note: Dietrich’s endless dragon combat is interpreted as divinely imposed penance.

The Devil.note: A demonic power carries Dietrich away on a black horse toward punishment.

The dragon.note: Beowulf confronts the treasure-guarding dragon with Wiglaf’s assistance.
Beowulf cuts the dragon open after Wiglaf strikes its underside.
The dragon bites Beowulf’s neck, and its venom causes his death.
The film makes the dragon Beowulf’s son by Grendel’s mother.
Sigemund kills the dragon alone with his sword and takes its hoard.

The nameless maiden in Wunderer.note: Dietrich saves the maiden from her cannibalistic pursuer.
The rescued maiden gives Dietrich a blessing connected with his final fate.

The Æsir.myth: Ragnar anticipates drinking with the Æsir
The Æsir.note: Ragnar’s dying poetic persona expects to drink ale among the Æsir.

The álfr.note: In Þiðreks saga, an unnamed supernatural álfr is Högni’s biological father.

Thora.note: Saxo’s Helgo rapes Thora and fathers Urse upon her.

Tófa.note: Tófa gives birth to Hervör I after Angantýr’s death.

Ubbi of Friesland.note: Ubbi fights Starkad and inflicts severe wounds upon him.

Unnr.note: Unnr, daughter of Freki, is Starkad’s mother in the Icelandic Víkar cycle.

Ute.note: German tradition makes Ute Gunther's mother.

Vingi.note: Atli's messenger deceives Gunnar and Högni into accepting the fatal invitation.

Virginal.note: Dietrich assists Virginal against Orkise, giants, and dragons.

Volker.note: Volker opposes Dietrich’s retainers during the hall battle.

Volker of Alzey.note: Volker serves as Gunther's minstrel-warrior and fights beside him.

Vǫlsungr.note: Signý is Vǫlsungr’s daughter and one of his two eldest twins.
Vǫlsungr accepts Siggeirr’s proposal despite Signý’s foreboding and enforces the pledged marriage.

Vǫlsungr.myth: Signý warns the Völsungs of Siggeirr’s ambush
Vǫlsungr.note: Vǫlsungr rejects Signý’s warning to retreat and orders her back to her husband.

Vǫttr.note: Vǫttr and Bödvar fight jointly among Hrólfr’s champions.

Walberan.note: Laurin’s powerful kinsman initially threatens Dietrich and his companions.
Dietrich’s party and Walberan eventually reach a settlement.

Walter.note: Gunnar pursues Walter for treasure; Walter defeats him and severs his leg.

Wenezlan.note: Dietrich fights the Polish king Wenezlan.

Widia.note: Widia rescues Theodoric from imprisonment among monsters.
Witege becomes Dietrich’s companion after challenging or being tested by him.
Dietrich pursues the deserter Witege after he kills Diether and Etzel’s sons.

Wieland.note: Wieland’s son Viðga and sword Mimung materially affect Dietrich’s combats.

Wisinus.note: Starkad kills the rapacious giant or champion Wisinus in Russia.

Wolfhart.note: Wolfhart is Dietrich’s fierce retainer and dies fighting the Burgundians.

Wunderer.note: Dietrich kills the cannibalistic Wunderer while protecting his intended victim.

Yrsa.note: Saxo’s Helgo fathers Urse upon Thora.
Saxo’s Helgo unknowingly has sex with his daughter Urse.

supernatural swallow.note: The magically sent bird hinders Egil while he composes his head-ransom poem.

the norns.note: Unnamed norns determine Helgi’s royal fame and stretch his golden fate-threads.

Áki.note: Áslaug curses Áki after revealing she knew he murdered Heimir.

Álfhildr.note: The abducted princess becomes the later Starkad’s paternal ancestress through Grímr and Stórvirkr.

Álfr.note: Helgi kills Álfr, a son of Hundingr, in battle.

Áli.note: Bjarki participates in warfare involving Áli and Aðils; his allegiance varies.

Ívarr inn beinlausi.note: Áslaug bears Ívarr after her warning about conception is disregarded.
Áslaug campaigns with Ívarr after urging vengeance for his half-brothers.

Ótryggr.note: The berserk Ótryggr mocks Starkad’s ugliness and giant ancestry.

Óðinn.note: Bödvar accompanies Hrólfr’s party while disguised Óðinn advises them.
Biarco suspects Óðinn aids the enemy and threatens to attack him.
Egil credits Óðinn with poetic power and the ability to expose deceivers.
Egil says he trusted Óðinn, but the god broke their friendship.
Óðinn enables Helgi’s death by lending Dagr the fatal spear.
Óðinn receives Helgi in Valhöll and offers him authority beside himself.
Óðinn, disguised as Hrani, offers Hrólfr weapons; Hrólfr refuses them and forfeits divine favor.

Óðinn.myth: Ragnar anticipates reception in Óðinn’s hall
Óðinn.note: Ragnar’s dying poetic persona expects Óðinn to prepare the hall for him.
Signý is Óðinn’s great-great-granddaughter through Sigi, Rerir, and Vǫlsungr.

Óðinn.myth: Sword planted in Barnstokkr at Signý’s wedding
Óðinn.note: Disguised, Óðinn plants the sword that provokes conflict between Sigmundr and Siggeirr.

Úlfr.note: The berserk Úlfr mocks Starkad’s ugliness and giant ancestry.

Þetleifr.note: Þetleifr joins Dietrich’s company of champions.
Dietleib helps Dietrich’s imprisoned party escape Laurin’s mountain realm.

Þorgerðr Hǫlgabrúðr.note: Modern scholars propose Lagertha may be a transformed version of Þorgerðr; the identification remains contested.

Þóra’s serpent.myth: Ragnar slays the serpent guarding Þóra
Þóra’s serpent.note: Ragnar kills Þóra’s guardian serpent using protective hairy clothing and wins her.

Þóra’s serpents.note: Ragnar kills the serpents with spear and sword while wearing frozen hairy garments.

Þórir Houndsfoot.note: Þórir Houndsfoot, king in Gautland, is Bödvar’s animal-marked brother.

Þórir of the hidden valley.note: The giant or half-troll hosts Grettir among his household.
